newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian stocks firm, led by preferred shares.
newsitem.headline: Russian stocks firm, led by preferred shares.

text.p: The Russian share market gained about one percent in hefty volumes on Tuesday, led by preferred shares and issues in second-tier stocks, traders said.

The Russian Trading System index closed at 190.20 after 188.74 on Monday on $30 million volume, which dealers said reflected the fact foreign investors had been unable to buy the stocks they wanted because of holidays in Russia and abroad since November 6.
The close was the highest for the RTS index since July 8.

"Sentiment is very positive, but the levels we are reaching are somewhere close to resistance for some blue chips and preferred shares," said Deutsche Morgan Grenfell trader Pavel Gronbjerg who saw the market bullish for the rest of the week.
"This may be one of the last rallies of the year."
Traders said foreign and domestic investors were buying.
Preferred shares were the top gainers, following a two-month trend of narrowing discounts for the issues, which have guaranteed dividends but no voting rights.
Rostelekom preferred, which rose to $2.202 from $2.20 at Monday's close, was seen continuing to rise on confidence in its dividend potential.
But dealers said preferred shares could face resistance as the price gap between them and ordinary stocks, which had been as high as 50-60 percent, narrowed to 20 or 30 percent.
Some preferred shares' recent rapid gains also reflected tight liquidity.
UCB chief trader Dmitry Ivenko said some oil company preferreds had the best case for growth.
"Since most oil holding companies don't have preferred shares, next year or later, when production companies shares are swapped into holding companies, the preferred discount will be lost."
Surgutneftegaz saw further gains on Monday's news that it had signed an ADR deal and that the government was investigating a share issue bought entirely by the Surgut holding company.

Common shares traded up to $0.440 from $0.424 on $7.2 million volume while preferred shares rose to $0.30 from $0.29, which dealers said reflected some movement to preferred shares against dilution risk from the new issue under review.
Dealers said that end-of-year profit-taking was not affecting the market.
But they said market tone was switching away from leading stocks such as Mosenergo towards less-frequently traded issues such as regional telecoms and utilities.
"Everyone wants to go into the second tier," said one senior Western trader.
Mosenergo finished the day at $0.994 after $0.978 on Monday. Norilsk Nickel preferred rose to $3.69 from $3.47 and common shares edged up to $6.38 from $6.36.
